messages:
maya: Heads-up — since ~03:10 UTC we've seen a spike in GPU pod evictions and a bunch of jobs stuck Pending in us-west2. Pods report 'Insufficient resources' but nodes look like they have freed GPUs. Suspect lease/heartbeat mismatch.

devon: saw the same. evict rate up ~3x for the last 20m. any networking flap in that AZ?

maya: no big BGP events in stackdriver. node heartbeats are intermittent in logs. attaching quick snippet.

maya: ```
    kubelet[1234]: WARN Failed to renew lease: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing
    kubelet[1234]: INFO lease renewed after retry
    kube-proxy[pid]: INFO conn reset to control-plane
    ```

liam: that looks like control-plane connectivity blips to the node agent. scheduler thinks the GPU is available because pod status moved, then kubelet reclaims it and eviction triggers?

anita: can someone paste the node labels/taints for one of the effected nodes? want to check GPU topology labels and any custom taints we use for dedicated pools.

devon: ran this: `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep us-west2-rack3` and `kubectl describe node us-west2-r3-node-22` — relevant bits below.

devon: ```
    Labels: gpu.family=nvidia-a100 gpu.count=8 topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west2-a
    Taints: dedicated=redwood:NoSchedule, gpu-reserved=true:NoExecute
    Conditions: Ready  (lastHeartbeatTime: 2m ago)
    Allocatable GPUs: 8, Allocated: 0 (temporary)
    ```

maya: Allocated showing 0 while pods Pending makes me think the scheduler removed the allocation due to lease timeout, then pods got scheduled elsewhere and evicted when kubelet reasserted the allocation. leads to double-scheduling and admission evictions.

anita: two quick mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily tighten the scheduler lease grace (so scheduler doesn't reassign too fast) or 2) increase warm-pool size in us-west2 and prefer burst capacity to avoid cross-AZ spill. But both have cost/complex tradeoffs.

liam: option 1 is lower-cost but could increase pending time if control-plane is flaky. option 2 is quick to buy time for customers. ops-bot, any insights from autoscaler?

ops-bot: autoscaler-alert: us-west2 GPU warm-pool at 12% free. Recent scale events: +3 nodes at 03:06 UTC, -1 node at 03:11 UTC. No failed launches.

devon: here's a proposal: roll a canary of kubelet/network-agent v2.1.3 with an added retry/backoff on lease RPCs (max jitter 5s). That should reduce transient double-claiming. we can route 5% of nodes in us-west2 to the canary.

maya: agree. also add a short-lived admission-controller guard to avoid scheduling onto nodes that have recent lease errors (<30s). simple patch.

anita: created an RFC in PR: https://redwood.dev/r/infra/lease-guard-canary — includes rollback plan, perf/cost impact table. If we do canary + warm-pool bump to 20% for 1h, we can avoid customer impact while observing.

liam: timeline? ops oncall can tarmac the warm-pool bump if PR approved.

devon: I'll open a small API ticket to temporarily increase warm-pool in us-west2 to 20% and pin for 60m. If canary looks good after 30m, we'll revert warm-pool to baseline.

maya: oncall: please run `kubectl get csidriver` and watch for flapping if any. Also keep an eye on eviction counts: `kubectl get events --field-selector reason=Evicted -A`

anita: adding cost note — bumping warm-pool by 8 nodes ~= +$4.2k/day. ops: only do the bump if we see customer-facing errors.

liam: i'll set an alert threshold: if evictions for gpu pods > 5/min for 10m -> auto-bump warm-pool and ping SRE pager.

devon: starting canary rollout now (5% nodes in us-west2). will post results in 15m.

maya: thanks. sharing a short postmortem stub in #postmortems once we have final root cause.

ops-bot: deploybot: canary rollout initiated for node-agent v2.1.3 -> 5% (us-west2).

anita: if anyone sees weird double-scheduling logs, paste them here. we should capture both scheduler decisions so we can correlate timestamps.

liam: 15m update: canary nodes show downstream lease retries but no evictions so far. eviction rate for the cluster dropped ~65%. keeping canary running.

maya: great. follow-up: let's make a post-deploy task to evaluate reducing the scheduler aggressive reassignment to avoid future thrash.

devon: noted. i'll create a follow ticket for packer/scheduler config tuning.

ops-bot: alert cleared: gpu-eviction-rate returned to baseline.

maya: closing loop — canary successful, warm-pool bump not required. moving to postmortem and perf follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
